demonstration: Paper test: human reviews target revision R, another action advances to R2, agent submits a modified patch under old approval. Required rejection/review principle is clear; exact message/evidence protocol remains missing.

title: Quality acceptance lacks measurable workloads and platform thresholds

sources.quote: ## Pass/fail or measurement thresholds

Records carry unitKind (sentence, paragraph or section), independent of the transformation kind and direction. Sentence labels remain inline. Paragraph/section rows reserve 22px above their source line and reuse the same glyphs, individual actions, 1500 ms tooltip delay and source-neutral selection behavior. # Acceptance and Conformance

problem: Some interaction details are precise (desktop widths, source-neutral widgets and tooltip delay), while generic assurance sections defer performance, accessibility and platform thresholds. Exact UI constraints are owner requirements, not defects; their repetition across levels increases maintenance cost when no single current assurance matrix exists.
consequences: A feature can pass examples yet have no agreed latency, workload size, keyboard/screenreader or failure budget. Repeated presentation details may drift while major quality risks remain unmeasurable.
demonstration: The testing strategy explicitly forbids fabricated benchmark/WCAG/platform claims and provides generic threshold text. Existing synthetic desktop evidence is valuable but narrower than full quality acceptance.
alternative_interpretations: Early local scope may intentionally prioritize source correctness over performance and broad platform support. Do not manufacture numerical targets.
possible_remedies: Create a small owner-reviewed quality scenario matrix: input size, concurrent contexts, operation, environment, required behavior and measurement; keep detailed presentation values in one source with cross-references.
tradeoffs: Premature hard targets can constrain implementation without user value. Choose workloads from actual use and clearly label observations versus acceptance thresholds.
next_action: Agree first supported workloads and accessibility scenarios before scale/conformance claims.
owner_approval: Yes for new acceptance thresholds; measuring current behavior is routine.
likelihood: Coverage gap certain; practical dissatisfaction unknown.

sources.needle: No claim is made that process exits exhaust power-loss

sources.quote: 4. Upgrading a schema-1 workspace requires a separately invoked enrollment/upgrade action while unlocked. Create and verify a consistent encrypted SQLite backup with restrictive permissions before the transaction. Preserve all existing encrypted record bytes and logical history. Add the table and change `user_version` atomically; do not upgrade merely by opening a file. Define explicit readers for supported schema 1 and 2; future/unknown versions

Durability assumes local filesystem, functioning SQLite VFS/fsync and storage hardware. No network filesystem support. Newly created file is create-only with restrictive permissions on Unix; reject symlink opens where supported. Parent directories must be user-controlled; no claim against a malicious same-user host. Consistent backup requires SQLite backup API; copying a live database or just ignoring WAL is unsupported. Portable `.hpxz`/`.hpx.js

problem: Process-exit injections show transaction-boundary behavior under the tested filesystem. They do not exhaust disk-full, fsync/VFS errors, torn storage, damaged backup, credential loss or restoration to a new trusted environment. Enrollment’s verified encrypted backup is a useful narrow increment, not a complete recovery product.
consequences: Acknowledged data durability is conditional on the local storage stack; users lack a fully specified general restore procedure. Failure to distinguish these scopes can overstate survivability.
demonstration: Read the explicit filesystem/hardware assumptions and narrow backup evidence. No hardware/power-loss or corrupt-backup experiment is executed in this review.
alternative_interpretations: SQLite/FULL and OS guarantees can be reasonable assumptions for the first slice; exhaustive fault simulation is not always cost-effective.
possible_remedies: Specify supported failure envelope and an isolated backup/restore rehearsal with missing/corrupt key wrapper, truncated backup, disk-full/fsync failure and process restart outcomes. Preserve originals and distinguish unavailable from irrecoverable data.
tradeoffs: Fault-injection adapters and platform testing cost effort; portable recovery must also avoid granting historical keys beyond intended recipients.
next_action: Before real-data recovery claims, select a minimal supported restore design and evidence plan.
owner_approval: Yes for recovery guarantees, format and credential policy; isolated analytical/fault tests are routine.
likelihood: Hardware failure likelihood unmeasured; evidence limit certain.
